dedupe_keys.name: open tyndp interfacing open energy system planning with entso e models

description: Open-TYNDP is an open-source model that reproduces and interfaces with the Ten-Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) process of the European transmission operators' association ENTSO-E, built on PyPSA-Eur. It is developed by Open Energy Transition with contributors including Thomas Gilon, Daniel Rüdt, Jonas Hörsch, Carlos Gaete-Morales, Elisabeth Zeyen, Will Usher and Maximilian Parzen, so that the official European grid planning scenarios can be examined and extended with open tools. Benchmarking against the TYNDP 2024 cycle is complete with results published online, and work is moving to the TYNDP 2026 cycle. Recent versions added demand-side response with price bands, alternative sources of hydrogen reference grid data, patches for faulty demand profiles using market model outputs, central carrier mappings and an archive of source data sets. Coverage is Europe. The code is accessible on GitHub and archived on Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost, and is very active (version 0.9 and 17 tags, latest commit September 2026). Caveats: the README warns it is not yet feature-complete and only the National Trends scenario is supported. Simulation uses are European transmission and hydrogen network planning and scenario analysis. Related records: model-pypsa-eur is its basis.
